findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics when the file cannot be read
findings.failure_mode: Missing or inaccessible shard file aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| MyError::Io(e))?

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics when the second CSV field is not a valid u32
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV data in any shard line causes a panic instead of returning a typed ParseError for that record
findings.fix: Use parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid) and propagate via Result, never unwrap

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use unchecked index access on a Vec built from split
findings.failure_mode: A CSV line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields causes an index-out-of-bounds panic; the bounds check is runtime and unbounded
findings.fix: Replace the split/collect/index pattern with line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) and bind the two fields directly

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy cast from u32; values in range (u16::MAX, u32::MAX] silently truncate
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value like 65536 parses successfully but silently truncates to 0, corrupting domain data without any error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) to reject out-of-range values with a typed error

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds console I/O inside the parsing closure that builds domain records
findings.failure_mode: Pure domain construction has a side-effect (stdout write) hidden inside what should be a calculation; breaks Functional Core / Imperative Shell, makes the function non-deterministic and untestable in isolation
findings.fix: Move all logging to the shell layer. The parse/calculation function should return pure Records with no println or other I/O

findings.problem: load_shards collects all lines into an unbounded Vec<Record> with no domain cap or try_reserve; also uses intermediate Vec<String> per line via split/collect
findings.failure_mode: A large or adversarial shard file causes unbounded heap allocation with no upper limit; no try_reserve and no bounded cap means memory exhaustion is possible before any domain logic runs
findings.fix: Validate a trusted max_rows cap before iteration; use Vec::new() then values.try_reserve(max_rows).map_err(|_| ParseError::Allocation)?; reject lines beyond the cap with a typed TooMany error

findings.problem: Record exposes name as String and value as u16 — raw primitives with no invariants encoded in the type
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct an invalid Record (empty name, value > u16::MAX via separate path) without the type system preventing it; illegal states are representable
findings.fix: Use newtypes for name (e.g. struct Name(String)) with a smart constructor, and encode value invariants in the type or use a checked constructor returning Result; make fields private behind a smart constructor
